name: aitp-console
//aitp: SDK floors that are load-bearing for THIS app, each with its consequence if violated -- same convention, and the same position, as `aitp-control-plane/package.json`'s `//aitp`: the rationale for a non-obvious version floor must live next to it or it is lost. This console is a *verifier*, never an issuer: the only two SDK symbols imported anywhere here are `verifyManifestJson` (`src/lib/api/verify-manifest.ts:1`) and `verifyRevocationList` (`src/lib/api/verify-revocation.ts:1`). That single fact is why this comment and CP's reach OPPOSITE conclusions about the same `0.12.0` release -- they are two correct answers to two different questions, not a stale note. `0.7.0`: the floor at which a `verifyManifestJson` failure first carries a typed `.code`; `verify-manifest.ts:22-23` and `verify-revocation.ts:6-9` both branch on `typeof code === 'string'`, and below this floor every failure would be misclassified as `sdk_unavailable`. `0.11.0`: NOT a floor here -- its one BREAKING entry (the pinned-key proof-timestamp erratum, RFC-AITP-0002 §3.1, `63f2223`) touches only `crates/aitp-handshake` plus the Rust adapter, and this console exposes no handshake endpoint. `0.12.0` (current, and LOAD-BEARING here -- this is where CP's answer and ours diverge): it fixes two false REJECTIONS that only a verifier can hit, both invisible to a surface diff. (1) `accepted_signature_algorithms` was not a member of `Manifest` until `crates/aitp-manifest/src/types.rs:57` at `aitp-v0.12.0` (absent at `c7a7159` and `aitp-v0.11.0`), and `Manifest` is `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` (`types.rs:11`), so on 0.10.0 an AUTHENTIC manifest carrying that spec-legal member threw `malformed` -- a false amber. (2) `Manifest::extensions` was a bare `ExtensionsMap` skipped via `skip_serializing_if = "ExtensionsMap::is_empty"` (`types.rs:62` at `c7a7159`) and became `Option<ExtensionsMap>` at `types.rs:93` in `0.12.0` (fix `b78e608`, not an ancestor of `aitp-v0.11.0`); `builder.rs:332-334` records the consequence verbatim: the old shape "silently dropped a wire-present `"extensions":{}` from the signing input -- a manifest signed with that literal shape failed verification." On 0.10.0 that is `signature_invalid`: a RED 'VERIFICATION FAILED' badge on an authentic artifact. CP is right that `0.12.0` is not load-bearing for IT, because CP is an issuer that builds through `ManifestOpts` (`bindings/aitp-node/src/agent.rs:36-57`), which exposes neither field and hard-codes `extensions: None` at `:414` -- so CP cannot emit either shape and cannot be bitten by either bug. A verifier does not choose what arrives on the wire. `0.12.0`'s other contents are NOT floors here, same as for CP: three new `ErrorCode` variants (`MANIFEST_INVALID`, `REVOCATION_SNAPSHOT_INVALID`, `REVOCATION_SNAPSHOT_SIGNATURE_INVALID`) and `IdentityDescriptor.extensions` are confined to the handshake/transport-http surface neither imported symbol touches. NON-CHANGE, recorded deliberately because two independent planning passes got it wrong in opposite directions: `0.12.0`'s `UnknownField` / `UNKNOWN_FIELD` work does NOT reach this console. Its only construction site is `parse_manifest_wire` (`crates/aitp-manifest/src/verifier.rs:174,181,185`), which has NO caller anywhere under `bindings/`; `verify_manifest_json` (`bindings/aitp-node/src/lib.rs:71-88`) calls `serde_json::from_str::<ManifestEnvelope>` then `verify_manifest` directly. And `deny_unknown_fields` sits on `Manifest` at `types.rs:11` at `c7a7159`, `v0.11.0`, `v0.12.0` AND `v0.13.0`. So a stray top-level member arrives as `malformed` before and after this bump -- unknown-member handling is an INVARIANT across the bump, not a tightening. Both Node entry points are byte-identical across the bump (`git diff c7a7159 aitp-v0.12.0 -- bindings/aitp-node/src/lib.rs bindings/aitp-node/src/revocation.rs` is empty), as is `index.d.ts` for both symbols: the surface is a trap, not a gate -- do not gate a future bump on a `.d.ts` diff. READING RELEASE BOUNDARIES: `aitp-rs/CHANGELOG.md` is useless for this -- it has no `## [0.11.0]`, `## [0.12.0]` or `## [0.13.0]` header at all; everything since `## [SDK 0.4.1]` sits under a never-rotated `## [Unreleased]`. Read the git tags instead -- AND check `bindings/aitp-node/package.json` at the tag before treating it as an npm release, because a tag here is not necessarily one: at tag `aitp-v0.10.0` the Node binding reads `0.5.0` and the tagged commit is titled 'chore: release v0.9.0 (#120)'. The real npm-0.10.0 tree is `c7a7159`; tags and npm agree from `aitp-v0.11.0` on. RANGE CHOICE `^0.12.0`, matching CP exactly: on a 0.x range npm's caret pins the MINOR, so only `0.12.x` patches float and a `0.13.0` needs a deliberate human edit. That is not pre-emptive caution -- `0.13.0` is ALREADY PUBLISHED (tagged 2026-09-23, and npm `latest`) and is being deliberately declined, which costs this console nothing: `git diff aitp-v0.12.0 aitp-v0.13.0` leaves `crates/aitp-tct/src/` and `crates/aitp-manifest/src/` untouched and `bindings/aitp-node/src/` unchanged, and `30b673b`'s `fix!` retaxonomy lands in `aitp-transport-http`, which the Node binding does not use (`bindings/aitp-node/src/revocation.rs:18-21` binds `aitp_tct`). The honest cost, stated: CP escapes the caret trap via 'the bump-aitp workflow'; THIS repo has no such workflow, so a caret here is a floor nobody automatically raises. That is the smaller cost. This repo sat on an unbounded `>=0.7.0` and still resolved `0.10.0` for two minors while shipping both false rejections above undetected -- the lockfile, not the range, decides what is installed, so the unbounded range bought no currency at all, only unreviewed forward consent. The compensating control for the caret is this comment plus the `PROGRESS.md` entry.
